https://forest-partnership.eu/jointcall2.texto:
FORESTPathways brings together 36 research funding organisations from 27 countries to support collaborative research and innovation for resilient forests and sustainable forest-based futures
Entitled FORESTPathways – Building Knowledge and Solutions for Resilient Forests and Sustainable Forest-Based Futures, the call brings together 36 Research Funding Organisations from 27 countries, with an indicative total public funding commitment of up to €40 million, including the European Union co-contribution.
FORESTPathways is an important first step in translating the ambitions of the FOREST Partnership into concrete action. By bringing together funding organisations and research communities across countries and connecting research communities across disciplines and sectors, this first Joint Call creates a unique opportunity to generate the knowledge, innovations and collaborations needed for resilient forests and a sustainable and a sustainable and competitive forest-based sector.
Annex VI – List of research performing beneficiaries of the FOREST Partnership (INFO 07.10.26: ALL RPOs that are not direct beneficiaries/partners of the FOREST Partnership may participate in the Joint Call as applicants without any restriction from this annex. RPOs that are direct beneficiaries/partners of the FOREST Partnership are subject to the restrictions set out in this Annex to ensure a fair and level playing field.)
INFORMATION WEBINAR: A webinar was hosted on 17.09.2026 (10:00 CET) for interested applicants. The webinar provided an overview of relevant aspects of the Call and a short introduction to the submission and evaluation system. The webinar slides and recording are now available here: https://forest-partnership.eu/information-webinar-on-the-forest-partnership-joint-call-2026-forestpathways/
NETWORKING WEBINAR: On 06.10.2026 (10:00 CET) the FOREST partnership organises a networking webinar providing stakeholders a chance to connect and network with each other enabling consortia establishments. Please register here: Registration is now closed. Webinar full.
These FAQs are intended to provide clarification of the published FOREST Joint Call 2026 documentation. They do not replace or amend the Call Announcement or its Annexes, which remain the authoritative sources for the Call requirements. Applicants must also consult the relevant national or regional funding regulations, as additional eligibility conditions may apply.
The Call Announcement does not explicitly restrict research activities to forests located within Europe.
However, proposals must address the objectives and scope of the Joint Call. Where research activities are proposed outside Europe, applicants should clearly demonstrate their relevance to the selected research topic and the objectives of the Partnership.
The eligibility of such activities and associated expenditure is subject to the national or regional funding regulations of the participating Research Funding Organisations. Applicants should therefore consult their relevant funders before submitting a proposal.
The four research topics establish the scope and objectives of the Joint Call. The research areas and examples included in the topic descriptions are intended to illustrate the scope rather than provide an exhaustive list of eligible activities.
Applicants should select the primary topic that best reflects the focus of their proposed research and clearly demonstrate how their proposal addresses its objectives.
The Call Office cannot provide advance approval or scientific assessment of individual research concepts and the respective selection of the call topic. Applicants should also consult the relevant national or regional funding regulations for any additional thematic restrictions.
Additional national or regional restrictions may apply, and applicants should consult Annex IV.
An Associated Partner contributes to project activities without requesting funding from a participating Research Funding Organisation. Associated Partners must meet the requirements set out in the Call Announcement, including providing the relevant commitment letters. They cannot coordinate a proposal or count towards the minimum consortium requirements.
No. The research areas listed under each topic are not intended to be a checklist. Applicants are not required to address every area or a particular number of them.

If you are a citizen of a country outside the EU/EEA or Switzerland, and believe you might qualify for a tuition fee exemption due to permanent residency in Norway or other ties to Norway, you should still contact us and apply for exemption.
Why do I need to apply even though it is clear that I am eligible for an exemption?
If you have been employed at NTNU for less than 24 months, you must provide documentation demonstrating other reasons why you might be eligible for an exemption from paying tuition fees.
Applicants to international master degree programmes:
If you are admitted to a study programme, your admission letter will state how much you are required to pay in tuition fees.
Applicants to Norwegian-language study programmes:
You will not receive information about the price in your admission letter. You can check the prices yourself on our website.
We have a large number of applicants to our Norwegian-language study programmes. To ensure that you have enough time to either apply for an exemption or pay the tuition fee before the start of the semester, we send the invoice and the information about the exemption option at the same time.
If the Norwegian Directorate of Immigration (UDI) rejects your application for a study permit to Norway, you will be refunded everything you have paid, except bank fees. The money will be transferred to your bank account in your home country. This applies in all cases, also after September 1st, provided that the rejection can be documented with the official decision letter from UDI.
If you have dual citizenship and one of the citizenships is from the EU/EEA or Switzerland, you do not have to pay tuition fees. You need to check which citizenship you are registered with at NTNU. If you need to "switch" citizenship with NTNU, you must submit a copy of your passport from the EU/EEA or Switzerland.
If one of your citizenships is a Norwegian citizenship, you do not have to pay tuition fees. You need to check which citizenship you are registered with at NTNU. If you need to "switch" citizenship with NTNU, you should send an email to opptak@ntnu.no to let us know that you are a Norwegian citizen. We can then verify against the national registry that you hold Norwegian citizenship.
This is because your basis for residence may have changed during an academic year. If you have residency based on family immigration, the basis for your residence, and thus the exemption from tuition fees, may be lost if the person you have residency with has left Norway. If you have residency based on marriage to a Norwegian citizen, we need to verify that your marital status has not changed since the previous academic year. The same applies if you have residency as a family member of an EU/EEA citizen residing in Norway. In that case, we need to verify that this citizen is still residing in Norway and has not left the country. Because the basis for residence can change for many applicants, we request that you reapply each year.
If you apply for admission to Norwegian courses at NTNU after autumn 2023, you must pay for the Norwegian course. Each level of the Norwegian course requires new admission. Even if you have completed, for example, NFUT 1 or 2 before autumn 2023, you must now pay for the Norwegian course if you intend to take new levels after autumn 2023. If you might be eligible for an exemption, you must submit an exemption application.
I have not received an invoice. I am not a citizen of the EU/EEA or Switzerland, but think I am eligible for an exemption. What Should I do?
If you are a citizen of a country outside the EU/EEA or Switzerland and might be eligible for an exemption, you still need to notify and submit an application for exemption with the required documentation.

funded consortia (2-4 partners each)
Participation is open to any legal entity, regardless of its type or profile (including but not limited to SMEs, large enterprises, universities, research and technology organisations, clusters, and public bodies).
Consortium structure (mandatory requirement)
Proposals must be submitted by a Consortium of 2 to 4 Legal Entities.

For complete guidelines, eligibility rules & submission criteria, click here.
Applicants are strongly advised not to rely solely on the auto-save feature and to draft and back up all answers in an external document (e.g., a text file) prior to filling out the form.
The BIOECONOMY GIANTS consortium accepts no responsibility or liability for any loss of unsubmitted data, lost progress, or any resulting consequences.
Once the Application is submitted via the online form, applicants will no longer have the possibility of modifying it.
One Application per Consortium
Only one Application must be submitted per consortium and an applicant (single legal entity) may participate in only one proposal.
Eligibility and Admissibility Check
Consortium Capacity and Budget Efficiency
The Open Call has a total budget of €280,000 and will fund up to four pilot projects. Each selected consortium can receive up to €70,000, with a maximum of €60,000 per participating legal entity. Funding is provided as a lump sum covering 100% of eligible costs.
Can an organisation apply individually, or is a consortium required?
A consortium is mandatory. Each application must be submitted by a national or transnational consortium consisting of a minimum of two and a maximum of four partners. One partner must be designated as the Lead Applicant.
Yes. Each consortium must include at least one eligible primary producer or related actor, as defined in Section 4.2 of the Open Call. Eligible profiles include individual farms, relevant agricultural and forestry businesses, farmers’ and forestry cooperatives, producer organisations and other categories specified in the call.
Can a consortium include more than one primary producer?
Yes. Each consortium must include at least one eligible primary producer or related actor, but more than one can participate, provided that the consortium consists of a minimum of two and a maximum of four partners.
Do consortium partners need to be established in different countries?
No. Both national and transnational consortia are eligible, provided that all partners meet the geographical and other eligibility requirements.
No. Beneficiaries, affiliated entities and partner organisations of the BIOECONOMY GIANTS consortium are excluded from participating in Open Call 2 to avoid potential conflicts of interest.
No. A legal entity may participate in only one proposal under Open Call 2. If an organisation participates in multiple proposals, all related applications will be declared ineligible. The same applies to duplicate or substantially similar proposals.
What types of projects are eligible for funding?
Eligible projects must focus on the piloting or scaling-up of high-added-value bio-based products through the valorisation of secondary or underutilised agricultural, agri-food or forestry biomass.
The proposed solution must be within the TRL 6–8 range at the time of application. Applicants must justify their current TRL and explain the technological progress expected during the seven-month implementation period. Projects are not required to progress from TRL 6 to TRL 8. The expected advancement should be realistic and measurable.
Does the cooperative business model need to be fully established before applying?
No. Applicants may propose cooperative business and governance arrangements that are already in place or that will be developed, adapted, tested or strengthened during the project. However, proposals must clearly explain the intended cooperation mechanisms, the roles of participating actors and how primary producers will participate in decision-making and benefit from the value generated.
Are projects focusing on the blue economy, aquaculture residues, marine side streams or bioenergy eligible?
Regarding bioenergy, proposals focusing solely or primarily on energy or biofuel production (e.g. heat, electricity, biogas or biofuels) are not eligible. However, bioenergy may be included as a complementary component of a broader project focused on developing high-added-value bio-based products, provided that the proposal meets all other scope and eligibility requirements.
